nodes.name: Real openings only
nodes.notes: This feed mixes two things: companies hiring, and freelancers offering themselves. Without this filter most alerts would be competitors, not jobs.

nodes.name: LinkedIn alerts
nodes.notes: Reads the job-alert emails LinkedIn sends you. It does NOT scrape LinkedIn: the inbox is yours. newer_than:2d stops it re-reading history every hour.

nodes.name: Extract the jobs
nodes.notes: The link is stripped of tracking on purpose: with the original tokens the dedupe would treat the same job as new every hour.

nodes.name: Himalayas
nodes.notes: Worldwide remote job board. 100 jobs per read.

nodes.name: We Work Remotely
nodes.notes: Remote job board. Its title arrives as 'Company: Role'.

nodes.name: Get on Board
nodes.notes: Public API, no credential needed. Verified 2026-08-08: HTTP 200.

nodes.name: Normalize LatAm results
nodes.notes: The three searches overlap; the Set keyed by URL avoids scoring — and paying for — the same job twice.

nodes.name: In my lane only
nodes.notes: This is the cost control. General boards return ~200 jobs an hour, almost all from other fields. Without this filter each one costs an LLM call and a small monthly cap is gone in days. The regex is deliberately broad: it drops the obvious, the model decides the rest. >>> REPLACE with the keywords of your own field.

nodes.name: Only what I haven't seen
nodes.notes: Stores the links already sent. Without this the same jobs would arrive every hour.

nodes.name: Repair model
nodes.notes: Only fires when the scoring model returns malformed JSON. Without it, one bad response kills the whole run.

messageValues.message:
You score job postings from 0 to 10 for how well they fit one candidate.

>>> EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS AN EXAMPLE. REPLACE IT WITH YOUR OWN PROFILE.
>>> Be specific: vague profiles produce vague scores. Name the tools, the
>>> industry and the seniority you actually have.

WHO THE CANDIDATE IS
- 6 years running operations in <industry> for the <market> market.
- Deep knowledge of: <the three or four things you genuinely know>.
- Also builds: <your technical stack>.
- <Language levels>. Lives in <city, COUNTRY>. Remote only.
- Targets: <role 1>, <role 2>, <role 3>.

THE RULE THAT OVERRIDES EVERY OTHER ONE: CAN THEY ACTUALLY HIRE THIS PERSON?
The candidate lives in <COUNTRY> and is not relocating. The question is not what
country the company is in, but WHERE THE PERSON IN THIS ROLE IS ALLOWED TO LIVE.

WORKS (no cap): Worldwide, Anywhere, Global, Remote with no country named, a
region that includes <COUNTRY>, <COUNTRY> itself, or any country list that
includes it. Also when the posting says nothing about location.

DOES NOT WORK (hard cap of 4): any restriction to a country or region that does
NOT include <COUNTRY>. It does not matter which country it is. Also capped:
"remote within <country>", "must be authorized to work in <country>", "hybrid",
"on-site", and any named city as headquarters.

WATCH THIS TRAP: "remote" does NOT mean they accept <COUNTRY>. "Remote from
<other country>" is remote AND excludes the candidate. If a country name that is
not <COUNTRY> appears next to the word remote, that IS a geographic restriction.
Never write "no geographic restriction" about a posting where you just named a
country.

The cap is a ceiling, not a deduction: a role that cannot hire them is not worth
their time even if it describes their entire career. If the location genuinely
is not mentioned anywhere, do not assume exclusion — score on content.

HOW TO SCORE (within what the cap allows)
- 9-10: <your exact intersection — the rarest combination you offer>.
- 7-8: strong on one of your two axes.
- 4-6: technical but generic, or asks for experience you do not have.
- 0-3: different field, or someone OFFERING services rather than hiring.

RAISE the score when the posting names <your keywords>.
LOWER the score when it asks for <the requirements you clearly do not meet>.

The reason goes in one sentence, direct, no filler. No "this opportunity
represents": say why it fits or why it does not. If the geographic cap applied,
open the sentence by naming the country that blocks it.

nodes.name: Score the job
nodes.notes: If this fails, the run continues: better an alert with no score than a lost job.

nodes.name: Worth it
nodes.notes: Only 7 and above pass. If the score is missing because the model failed, it passes too: better to review it by hand than lose it.
